intent: To explain the construction and structure of a population pyramid by organizing a population by age and separating it by gender.

requirements.question: Must the video show single-year ages from 1 to 100, or can it use age groups?
Is the overall young-high/old-low shape required, or is only the age/gender breakdown required?

units.claim: The age dimension covers single years from 1 to 100, ordered by age, so each age has a row for each gender.
accept: The data covers single years of age across the full range
Every age from 1 through 100 appears for male and female
units.evidence: The chart must show or label an age progression spanning 1 to 100, not just a few aggregated age bands.

units.claim: The values are largest at the youngest ages and smallest at the oldest ages: the youngest ages reach 73 squares while the oldest ages are around 3 squares.
accept: Values decline from youngest to oldest ages
The youngest ages are much larger than the oldest ages
The series shrinks from about 73 squares at the youngest to about 3 squares at the oldest
units.evidence: The chart must show a clear overall gradient from high values at the young end to low values at the old end.

optional_valid: The unit of the values is squares, with the maximum 73 squares and minimum 3 squares.
Relative_value is 1.0000 at the maximum 73-square rows and about 0.0411 at the minimum 3-square rows.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
